subject: general
question: What is the normal systolic and diastolic pressure in humans?

options.text: 120 mm of Hg / 80 mm of Hg
120 mm of Hg / 90 mm of Hg
130 mm of Hg / 90 mm of Hg
130 mm of Hg / 80 mm of Hg

solution:
The correct answer is __**120 mm of Hg / 80 mm of Hg.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The normal systolic and diastolic pressure in humans is 120 mm of Hg / 80 mm of Hg.**
 
• Blood is pushed through the arteries to the rest of the body when the heart contracts during each beat. 
 
• The term "**systolic blood pressure**" refers to this. Systolic blood pressure should not exceed 120 mm Hg.
 
• When the heart is between **beats or diastole**, the blood pressure in the arteries is measured. 
 
• When a person's health changes, or when they engage in particular activities like sports or exercise, their **systolic and diastolic pressure** will vary. Afterwards, the pressure will return to normal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood Pressure**

 
 
• **Blood pressure** readings that are less than **120/80 mm Hg **are regarded as normal.
 
• If your outcomes fall within this category, keep up heart-healthy routines like eating a balanced diet and exercising frequently.
 
• **Systolic blood pressure**, or the first number, is typically given more consideration as a significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease in adults over 50.
